text: The Crimean (Kerch) Bridge is two parallel structures, a four-lane road bridge and a double-track rail bridge, about 19 km long, across the Kerch Strait.
Russia built the Crimean Bridge after occupying Crimea in 2014; it opened to cars in May 2018 and to trains in December 2019.
After the October 2022 explosion, the Crimean Bridge road fully reopened on 23 Feb 2023 and the rail bridge on 5 May 2023, per Russian official dates.
According to RUSI, no heavy trucks cross the Crimean Bridge in 2026 and all three Kerch Strait ferries have been struck.
Crimea is being "turned into an island" by 2026.
The Crimean Bridge always reopened after each Ukrainian strike; destroying it outright is not a historical outcome.
notes: OUTCOME; the win condition in every act is damage inside the historical band followed by the bridge reopening

text: The SBU says Ukraine hit the Crimean Bridge three times, each by a different route: first from land, second from the water, and in 2025 from underneath the water.

cites.quote: The first time we approached it from land, the second time – from the water. In 2025, we approached it from underneath the water

text: On 8 Oct 2022 at 06:07 a truck carrying a concealed charge exploded on the Crimea-bound road lanes of the Crimean Bridge, dropping road spans into the strait and setting fire to fuel tank cars of a freight train on the rail bridge alongside.
Ukrainian sources named the SBU as behind the 8 Oct 2022 Crimean Bridge explosion the same morning.
The SBU confirmed in July and August 2023 that it was behind the October 2022 Crimean Bridge explosion.
Two days after the 8 Oct 2022 bridge explosion, Putin called the 10 Oct 2022 missile and drone strike on Ukrainian energy and cities retaliation for the bridge.
On the night of 17 Jul 2023 two SBU Sea Baby surface drones, in a joint operation with the Ukrainian Navy, struck the Crimean Bridge; one road span collapsed and an adjacent span was knocked loose.
Between the July 2023 and June 2025 strikes, Russia surrounded the Crimean Bridge with sunken ferries, barge lines, booms, nets, "hedgehogs", smoke and patrol craft.
Storms broke the Russian barrier around the Crimean Bridge more than once.
On 3 Jun 2025 the SBU set off charges that its agents had placed at the Crimean Bridge's underwater supports over several months, going under the barrier rather than through it.
In 2026 the Crimean Bridge still stands but carries no heavy trucks, and the Kerch Strait ferries that replaced it for dangerous cargo have been struck out of service.
In Act 1 (8 Oct 2022), two road spans of the Crimea-bound carriageway of the Crimean Bridge fell into the water and a third was damaged.

In 2026 the Crimean Bridge is open but with frequent overnight closures and queues of up to 2,500 vehicles.
In October 2017 Rosgvardia announced a new "maritime brigade" to protect the Crimean Bridge.
The Crimean Bridge road section opened to cars on 16 May 2018, with trucks allowed from 1 Oct 2018.
The Crimean Bridge rail section opened on 23–25 Dec 2019, with freight trains from 30 Jun 2020.
In spring 2022 the SBU began considering an operation against the Crimean Bridge.
In June 2022 Maj Gen Dmytro Marchenko called the Crimean Bridge "target number one".
On 1 Jul 2022 Russia tested a smokescreen over the Crimean Bridge, while two target barges with radar reflectors sat on its east side.

Per the Russian case file, on 4 Oct 2022 the bomb cargo crossed into Russia at Verkhny Lars in a DAF truck.
Per the Russian case file, on 6 Oct 2022 the cargo reached Armavir and was reloaded onto an International ProStar truck driven by Makhir Yusubov, who did not know what it was.
On 7 Oct 2022, Putin's 70th birthday, Makhir Yusubov collected the load for Simferopol, then stopped on the Russian side to sleep.
At about 06:00 on 8 Oct 2022 the truck passed inspection at Taman: the cargo bay was opened, but it was not put through the X-ray.
At 06:05–06:07 on 8 Oct 2022 Crimea Railway detected a fault and a fuel tank car on the Crimean Bridge caught fire.
At 06:07 on 8 Oct 2022 the truck exploded on the Crimea-bound road lanes of the Crimean Bridge; per the case file it was set off by a GPS trigger at km 156 of the Novorossiysk–Kerch road.
At 10:55 on 8 Oct 2022 Ukrainska Pravda reported, citing a law-enforcement source, that the Crimean Bridge explosion was an SBU special operation; the SBU did not comment.
Planet and Maxar imagery of the Crimean Bridge damage was published on 8 Oct 2022.
On 8 Oct 2022 a Putin decree put Crimean Bridge security under the FSB, and Surovikin was named commander of the Russian operation in Ukraine.
During the day on 8 Oct 2022 one Crimean Bridge carriageway reopened to cars and buses after checks; trucks had to use the ferry, and rail traffic restarted that evening.
From 8 Oct 2022 Russia relaunched the Kerch ferry; it took 16 trucks at a time, and a week later trucks waited 3–4 days.

text: On 12 Aug 2023, in two waves at about 13:00 and 15:00, the Crimean Bridge was attacked; Russia claimed S-200 missiles were downed (two, then a third), at least eight explosions were heard, and the bridge was covered in smoke that Russia called a screen.

On 22 Aug 2023 HUR said Russia was sinking ferries in front of the Crimean Bridge: one sunk and at least six planned.
Planet imagery of 29 Aug 2023 shows seven partly sunk vessels in a line just south of the Crimean Bridge, about 160 m apart.

On 14 Oct 2023 all four Crimean Bridge road lanes reopened, "ahead of schedule".
On 25 Nov 2023 an SBU documentary series declared: "The bridge is doomed."
A storm on 26–27 Nov 2023 wrecked the boom barges at the Crimean Bridge: three flooded, one partly, two washed away and one adrift.
In March 2024 the patrol ship Sergey Kotov was sunk by Ukrainian USVs while guarding the southern approaches to the Crimean Bridge.

text: On 18 Mar 2024 Putin announced a Rostov–Sevastopol railway through occupied territory to give "redundancy for the Kerch bridge".
On 7 May 2024 work started on a new surface barrier at the Crimean Bridge; by 23 May seven barge sections were installed, each 90–100 m long.
On 14 Jun 2024 H I Sutton described the Crimean Bridge's defence layers: an outer barge line, booms and nets inside it, and towable barges to close the arch channel.
By the end of June 2024 a second barrier line of 21 barges was in place at the Crimean Bridge.
On 23 Jul 2024 Brady Africk imagery showed more than 30 barges at the Crimean Bridge.
From August 2024 "hedgehog" obstacles began to be sunk in the Kerch Strait, sometimes in two layers.
In mid-August 2024 a permanent structure went up alongside the Crimean Bridge, and a Pantsir-S1M was deployed on the bridge itself.
On 15 Aug 2024 Russia claimed it downed 12 ATACMS aimed at the Crimean Bridge, and that Mi-8 and Ka-29 helicopters killed five USVs.
There were 36 boom barges at the Crimean Bridge in October 2024; storms scattered them, fragments washed ashore in Kerch, and 17 were back by late January 2025.
In December 2024 5–6 guard vessels protected the Crimean Bridge, and its Black Sea side was fully boomed, with a retractable section and a duty tug at the shipping span.
The Russian bridge channel reported Crimean Bridge traffic suspended 04:00–07:00 on 3 Jun 2025, for about 3 hours, then normal.
On 3 Jun 2025 Navy spokesman Pletenchuk said the "key and most complex" part of the Crimean Bridge was damaged.
On 3 Jun 2025 the FSB said it detained an agent over the Crimean Bridge strike.
On 4 Jun 2025 Peskov acknowledged an explosion at the Crimean Bridge but said there was "no damage".
On 27 Nov 2025 a Rostov military court sentenced eight defendants to life for the 2022 Crimean Bridge bombing.
On 7 Jan 2026 the Crimean Bridge's Black Sea side was guarded by an Okhotnik patrol ship, two Grachonok boats and a Shmel.

The Crimean Bridge was closed 23:51–06:14 on 25–26 Jun 2026, with 2,500 vehicles waiting for manual checks.
The Crimean Bridge is a pair of separate, parallel bridges: a four-lane road of two two-lane carriageways and a double-track, unelectrified railway worked by diesel locomotives.
The Crimean Bridge's total length is about 19 km.
Summed OSM bridge ways give about 16.8 km of road per carriageway and about 18.1 km of rail for the Crimean Bridge (computed 2026-10-01).
The Crimean Bridge has three sea sections: Taman to Tuzla Spit, 7 km; across Tuzla Island, 6.5 km; Tuzla Island to Crimea, 5.5 km.
The Crimean Bridge's steel arches over the Kerch–Yenikale shipping canal span 227 m with 35 m clearance.
OSM tags the Crimean Bridge navigation span as a truss of length 227 with a 185 m clearance width; its centre is about 45.3086 N, 36.5060 E, roughly 2.3 km from the Crimean landfall (computed).
The Crimean Bridge stands on more than 7,000 piles driven up to 90 m below the water, some raked for earthquakes, through about 60 m of silt over a faulted bedrock.
Concrete piers carry the Crimean Bridge roadway and railway.
Crimean Bridge spans are short, a few tens of metres; the 2022 replacement road span was 64 m.
Crimean Bridge piers are numbered, as in "support 145" in 2023 and "supports 235 and 236" in 2022.
Cylindrical concrete fenders were reportedly built in front of the Crimean Bridge piers against ramming.
The Crimean road landfall of the Crimean Bridge, at Ak-Burun in Kerch, is at 45.324, 36.487 (OSM, computed).
The Ak-Burun locality in Kerch is at 45.317, 36.493 (Nominatim).

text: The Kerch ferry route runs north of the Crimean Bridge.
In late 2024 a parallel structure with air-defence platforms was under construction on the northern (Sea of Azov) side of the Crimean Bridge.
The Crimean Bridge is one of two southern ground lines of communication for Russian forces; the other runs through occupied Donetsk, Zaporizhzhia and Kherson oblasts.
After the October 2022 bridge explosion, Russian columns moved along Mariupol–Berdiansk–Melitopol.
After the July 2023 strike, tourist traffic from Crimea was rerouted through Dzhankoi and Armiansk toward Melitopol.
Russia built a rail line through the occupied coast as an alternative to the Crimean Bridge.
By 2026 the land corridor to Crimea was itself under drone attack: M-14 freight was down about 71%, and the Chonhar and North Crimean Canal crossings were cut.
Weather and light for the three Crimean Bridge attack days come from ERA5 reanalysis via Open-Meteo for grid cell 45.30 N 36.51 E (computed 2026-10-01).
At 06:07 on 8 Oct 2022 conditions at the Crimean Bridge were 16 °C, clear (0% cloud), with wind about 27 km/h from the ENE (about 55°) (ERA5).
Sunrise at the Crimean Bridge on 8 Oct 2022 was 06:40, so the 06:07 explosion came in twilight about 33 min before sunrise (computed).
At 03:04 / 03:20 on 17 Jul 2023 conditions at the Crimean Bridge were 24 °C, mostly clear, with wind about 11 km/h from the NNW (ERA5); sunrise was 05:01, so it was full night.
The Sea Baby drones that struck the Crimean Bridge on 17 Jul 2023 were guided by thermal camera in full night.
At 04:44 on 3 Jun 2025 conditions at the Crimean Bridge were 19 °C and clear, with wind 6–8 km/h from the W–WNW (ERA5); sunrise was 04:48, so it was dawn.
Wikipedia says a north wind blew the October 2022 fire and smoke from the Crimean Bridge toward the Black Sea, which the dossier finds consistent with the ERA5 northeasterly.
In Act 1 (October 2022) the SBU, led by acting head Vasyl Malyuk, carried out the Crimean Bridge attack.

The SBU's Act 1 means were one truck carrying RDX cylinders of 21 t TNT equivalent hidden in film rolls, and a way around the Crimean Bridge's GPS jammers; Malyuk says no foreign partners were involved.
Russia blamed HUR and Budanov for the October 2022 Crimean Bridge attack, which the SBU denied.
In Act 2 (July 2023) the SBU worked with the Ukrainian Navy, led by Malyuk and Adm Oleksii Neizhpapa, using two Sea Baby USVs carrying up to 850 kg each.
The Sea Baby drones used in July 2023 were built in an underground facility in Ukraine.
The August–September 2023 attacks on the Crimean Bridge are not attributed; Russia claimed S-200 missiles and semi-submersible USVs, and there is no Ukrainian confirmation.

In Act 3 (June 2025) the SBU, with its 13th Main Directorate of Military Counterintelligence and led personally by Malyuk, used two underwater charges of 1,100 kg TNT equivalent each, laid by agents over months.

mentions.name: SBU 13th Main Directorate of Military Counterintelligence

text: The delivery method of the June 2025 charges was not disclosed; Euromaidan infers underwater drones.
In the 2026 coda HUR's Active Operations Department, the Unmanned Systems Forces (Brovdi), the Ukrainian Navy and the SSO used drones against Kerch ferries and guard boats, and middle-strike drones.
Before October 2022, according largely to relayed Russian media claims, Rosgvardia units at both Crimean Bridge entrances had vehicle scanners, but checks were selective.
Before October 2022, FSB border units and anti-sabotage groups guarded the Crimean Bridge, per relayed Russian media claims.
Before October 2022, Grachonok and Mangust boats guarded the Crimean Bridge, with BK-16 assault boats if needed, per relayed Russian media claims.
Before October 2022, the Crimean Bridge defence reportedly included divers, the Plavnik and Amulet-P underwater systems, and "trained dolphins".
Before October 2022, the Crimean Bridge was reportedly covered by S-400 and Pantsir-S1, Bal and Bastion coastal missiles, and Su-27 and Il-38 patrols.
Before October 2022, Russia had two radar-reflector target barges at the Crimean Bridge and ran smoke trials.
After October 2022, security of the Crimean Bridge moved under the FSB.
After October 2022, Russia placed a Project 436BIS(R) target ship near the Crimean Bridge to decoy radar-homing missiles.
In July 2024 two boats were on constant guard at the Crimean Bridge.
In August–September 2024 a Pantsir-S1M stood on the Crimean Bridge itself.
In December 2024 5–6 Rosgvardia, FSB and Border Guard vessels guarded the Crimean Bridge, armed with AA guns, heavy machine guns, anti-sabotage grenade launchers and Vikhr missiles.
Russia claimed in August 2024 that Mi-8 and Ka-29 helicopters of the Black Sea Fleet's naval aviation hunt USVs at the Crimean Bridge.
The patrol ship Sergey Kotov guarded the southern approaches to the Crimean Bridge until it was sunk in March 2024.

In 2026 the Black Sea side of the Crimean Bridge was guarded by a Project 22460 Okhotnik FSB patrol ship, two Project 21980 Grachonok boats and a Project 1204 Shmel, with a Sobol patrol boat also present.
Smoke-generator vehicles were on the Crimean Bridge deck.
Deputy PM Marat Khusnullin ran the Crimean Bridge repair headquarters.
Nizhneangarsktransstroy held the 2022–23 Crimean Bridge repair contract.
In the Ukrainian account, the Act 1 truck bomb was RDX in metal cylinders, 21 t TNT equivalent, wrapped in packing film, and the cargo was declared as film rolls.
The SBU says it "calculated the thickness of the film layer needed to hide the explosives from custom scanners".

cites.quote: The Security Service calculated the thickness of the film layer needed to hide the explosives from custom scanners.

text: The SBU bypassed the Crimean Bridge's GPS jammers with "a technically sophisticated system" and set off the Act 1 charge mid-bridge.
The Russian case file says the Act 1 charge was about 10 t TNT equivalent of solid rocket fuel with a hexogen-type initiator, fired by a GPS navigator at a set point (km 156).
An X-ray scanner existed at the Crimean Bridge entrance in October 2022, but the bomb truck was not scanned.
After October 2022 Russia introduced heavier checks, FSB control and bans on fuel and ammunition on the Crimean Bridge.
Sea Baby is an SBU surface drone carrying up to 850 kg, with electro-optical and infrared cameras and a SATCOM dome.
The SBU credited Sea Baby with hitting the Olenegorsky Gornyak and the tanker SIG in August 2023.
In Act 2 the Sea Baby was guided by an operator from a thermal view and driven at a Crimean Bridge pier at speed in darkness.
In Act 2 two Sea Baby boats struck the Crimean Bridge from opposite directions about five minutes apart.
The July 2023 Sea Baby blast "lifted and then dropped a section of the road bridge".

cites.quote: lifted and then dropped a section of the road bridge

text: No floating or sunken barrier is reported at the Crimean Bridge before August 2023; only the claimed pier fenders, boats and divers of 2022.
After the July 2023 strike, milbloggers, Girkin among them, attacked the Russian authorities for guarding the road checkpoint rather than the sea.
From July 2022 Russia had two radar-reflector target barges on the east side of the Crimean Bridge and held a smoke trial, per TWZ imagery and video.
UK Defence Intelligence says radar-decoy barges were tested at the Crimean Bridge in September 2022.
Russian media, via Meduza, claimed that in 2022 the Crimean Bridge had concrete ram fenders (cylinders in front of piers), divers and acoustic and sonar systems; these did not stop Act 2.
From 24 May 2023 smoke generators were used on and around the Crimean Bridge deck, including on 12 Aug 2023, per UK Defence Intelligence.
Vantor imagery showed smoke-generator vehicles on the Crimean Bridge in June 2026.

From 22–29 Aug 2023 Russia placed 7 partly sunk hulls with booms between them in a line "just south of the bridge", about 160 m apart per UK DI, "a little more than a tenth of a mile" per TWZ, or about 200 m per Militarnyi.

text: HUR placed the 2023 block-ship line near Tuzla, at the southern section where Sea Baby struck; H I Sutton's post said "western approaches"; at least 6 ships were planned.
H I Sutton judged the block-ship line "moderately effective" against surface and underwater drones.
From late August 2023 boom barges (barrels linked with cables; empty tanks in frames) sat between the block-ship hulls at the Crimean Bridge.
The 26–27 Nov 2023 storm flooded, washed away or set adrift all seven boom barges at the Crimean Bridge; boom barges repeatedly washed ashore in Kerch.

From 7 May 2024 Russia moored barges end to end on the southern approaches in front of the main Crimean Bridge as an outer barge line: 7 sections of 90–100 m by 23 May and more than 30 barges by 23 Jul 2024 (Crimean Wind, Brady Africk).
Gaps in the Crimean Bridge barge line were closed by moving barges closer together.
From June 2024 towable "gate" barges were positioned to be towed forward to shut the channel under the Crimean Bridge arch.
From June 2024 an inner layer of nets and floating booms lay inside the barge line, parallel to the Crimean Bridge.
By the end of June 2024 a second barrier line of 21 barges was in place at the Crimean Bridge (Krym.Realii).

From June to August 2024 Russia built new piers either side of the smaller span south of the Crimean Bridge arch, then a permanent parallel structure alongside the bridge, and one on the Azov side with air-defence platforms; its purpose (road or barrier) is unclear.

From August 2024 Russia sank "hedgehogs" / metal "ruffs" on the seabed in 1–2 layers, laid by floating crane from barges, and from September 2024 put metal fences around the Crimean Bridge pillars (Crimean Wind).
UK intelligence reported naval mines and anti-USV nets at the Crimean Bridge in 2024.

From October 2024 to January 2025 a full boom ran across the Black Sea side of the Crimean Bridge, retractable at the shipping span with a duty tug: 36 boom barges in October 2024, 17 by late January 2025, as storms destroyed most of the 36.
Patrol boats, ships and helicopters guarded the Crimean Bridge from 2022; the Sergey Kotov was sunk in 2024 and a Sobol and a Grachonok were hit in 2026.
In Act 3 charges were placed at the Crimean Bridge supports over several months and fired starting at 04:44 on 3 Jun 2025.
The method used to place the June 2025 charges is undisclosed; Russian milbloggers guessed a sea drone.
Euromaidan inferred that underwater drones placed the June 2025 charges.
The Crimean Bridge barrier system was built against surface and underwater drones and did not stop charges laid by agents in 2025.
notes: the block's own synthesis; cited to the Act 3 source of the same section

text: After 2022, fuel and ammunition were barred from the Crimean Bridge and moved by ferry and landing ship.
The Crimean Bridge road weight limit was 3.5 t after the 2023 repair and 5 t in 2025.
The SBU in November 2023 described reverse-flow road traffic and wagon limits on the Crimean Bridge.
Every Crimean Bridge closure brings manual checks, queues of thousands and a 200-litre liquids rule.
When the Kerch ferries were destroyed in 2026, dangerous rail cargo may have had to return to the Crimean Bridge.

measure: Sea Baby surface drone attacks on the Crimean Bridge
effect: moderately effective against surface and underwater drones (Sutton)
rationale: After two Sea Babies hit the bridge in Jul 2023, Russia sank a line of block ships with booms between them just south of the bridge; Sutton judged it moderately effective against surface and underwater drones.

counter: outer barge line, inner booms and nets
measure: naval drone (USV) attacks on the Crimean Bridge
effect: physical barrier to surface drones; gaps closed by moving barges closer
rationale: From May 2024 Russia moored barges end to end on the southern approaches, with nets and floating booms inside, to stop sea drones that approach from the Black Sea side.

counter: towable gate barges at the arch
measure: naval drone passage through the Crimean Bridge shipping channel
rationale: Barges were positioned to be towed forward to shut the channel under the arch, the gap that a continuous barge line must leave for shipping.

counter: sunken hedgehogs / metal ruffs and pillar fences
measure: underwater and semi-submersible drone attacks on Crimean Bridge piers
rationale: From Aug 2024 hedgehogs were sunk on the seabed in 1–2 layers and metal fences put around the pillars; the barrier system was built against surface and underwater drones.

measure: missile and drone strikes on the Crimean Bridge
effect: obscures the bridge from optical guidance (screen)
rationale: Smoke generators were tested from 24 May 2023, used on 12 Aug 2023 when the bridge was covered in smoke Russia called a screen during claimed S-200 attacks, and smoke-generator vehicles stood on the deck in 2026.

counter: radar-reflector target barges and target ship
measure: radar-homing missile strikes on the Crimean Bridge
rationale: Two radar-reflector target barges sat east of the bridge from Jul 2022, radar-decoy barges were tested in Sep 2022, and a Project 436BIS(R) target ship was placed near the bridge to decoy radar-homing missiles.

measure: barge and boom barriers at the Crimean Bridge
effect: barrier repeatedly broken; Russia rebuilt it
rationale: The 26–27 Nov 2023 storm flooded, washed away or set adrift all seven boom barges, and storms in late 2024 destroyed most of the 36 boom barges, leaving 17 by late Jan 2025.

measure: surface and underwater drone barriers (barges, booms, nets, hedgehogs)
rationale: In Jun 2025 the SBU went under the barrier rather than through it, with charges its agents placed at the underwater supports over months; the barrier system built against drones did not stop them.

counter: film-roll concealment sized against X-ray scanners
measure: vehicle X-ray scanning at the Crimean Bridge checkpoint
rationale: The SBU calculated the film thickness needed to hide the explosives from customs scanners; at Taman the truck was opened but not X-rayed.

measure: GPS jamming on the Crimean Bridge
rationale: The SBU bypassed the bridge's GPS jammers with a technically sophisticated system and set off the charge mid-bridge.

counter: FSB control, heavier checks and fuel/ammunition ban
measure: truck bombs crossing the Crimean Bridge
rationale: After the Oct 2022 truck bomb, bridge security moved under the FSB, checks became heavier, and fuel and ammunition were barred from the bridge.

counter: weight limits and moving dangerous cargo to ferries and landing ships
measure: damage to the Crimean Bridge and risk to military logistics on it
rationale: Russia barred fuel and ammunition, imposed 3.5 t then 5 t weight limits, and moved dangerous cargo to ferries and ships; military trains fell from 42–46 a day to 4–5.

measure: ferry bypass of the Crimean Bridge for dangerous cargo
rationale: In 2026 Ukrainian drones disabled the rail ferries Slavyanin and Avangard and Operation MoLoCHKa cut ferry capacity by 75%, so dangerous rail cargo may have had to return to the bridge.

counter: Ukrainian USV and drone strikes on guard ships
measure: patrol ships and boats guarding the Crimean Bridge
rationale: The Sergey Kotov was sunk by Ukrainian USVs while guarding the southern approaches in Mar 2024, and the Navy hit a Sobol and a Grachonok guarding the bridge on 30 Apr 2026.

counter: patrol vessels and helicopters hunting USVs
measure: naval drone attacks on the Crimean Bridge
rationale: Russia claimed Mi-8 and Ka-29 helicopters killed five USVs on 15 Aug 2024 and that three semi-submersible drones were destroyed on 1–2 Sep 2023; none independently verified.

measure: air and missile strikes on the Crimean Bridge
rationale: A Pantsir-S1M was deployed on the bridge itself in mid-Aug 2024; Russia claimed 12 ATACMS aimed at the bridge downed on 15 Aug 2024.

text: At the Taman checkpoint at about 06:00 on 8 Oct 2022 a guard had the bay of the film-roll truck bound for Simferopol opened, glanced in and waved it on, while the X-ray portal stood unused; surveillance video later showed the driver "calm".
The SBU prepared the Act 1 operation for months: route, paperwork, and film thickness against the scanners.
At 06:07 on 8 Oct 2022 a car passed the truck as the road climbed toward the Crimean Bridge arch; a blinding flash put all four lanes in flames and two spans dropped into the strait.
On 8 Oct 2022 a fuel train burned on the Crimean Bridge rail section alongside, with smoke driven seaward by a northerly to northeasterly wind in pre-dawn twilight.
By the afternoon of 8 Oct 2022 light traffic crawled over the surviving Crimean Bridge carriageway while trucks waited days for a 16-truck ferry.
The 10 Oct 2022 Russian strike launched 84 cruise missiles and 24 drones across Ukraine and killed 19 people.
At 03:04 on 17 Jul 2023 the first Sea Baby, steered from a FLIR view, hit the Crimean Bridge road section; about five minutes later a second came in from the other side toward the rail section.
In the July 2023 strike a Crimean Bridge span lifted and dropped.
On the afternoon of 12 Aug 2023 explosions were heard at the Crimean Bridge, Russia claimed downed S-200s, and white smoke-generator plumes mixed with black smoke over the bridge.
In 2023 seven half-sunk ferries lay in a dotted line south of the Crimean Bridge with booms strung between them.
In late November 2023 a storm tore most of the Crimean Bridge block-ship and boom barrier apart.
In 2024 the Crimean Bridge defence comprised an outer chain of barges, then booms and nets, sunken hedgehogs, a towable gate at the arch, a Pantsir on the deck and patrol boats.
At 04:44 on 3 Jun 2025 the SBU's video shows a column of water erupting beside a Crimean Bridge pier.
The 3 Jun 2025 Crimean Bridge strike came two days after Operation Spiderweb.
In 2026 the last Kerch rail ferry burned at sea and ferries were towed as barges.
In 2026 ten-kilometre queues formed at the Crimean Bridge approaches, and smoke vehicles stood on the deck.

observations.subject: vehicle queue length at the approaches

text: In spring–summer 2022 the SBU first considered using freight cars on the Crimean Bridge railway; after Russia restricted non-military cargo on the rail bridge, the SBU switched to a truck.
The SBU chose film-roll cover sized against scanners and a long indirect route for the Act 1 cargo.
Per Russian investigators the Act 1 cargo route ran Odesa → Ruse → Poti → Yerevan → Verkhny Lars → Armavir, using unwitting carriers.
Malyuk said of the Act 1 operation: "we used so many people without their knowledge".

cites.quote: we used so many people without their knowledge

text: At the Crimean Bridge entrance in October 2022 Russian guards chose to inspect the bomb truck by hand but did not scan it on the X-ray.
After the October 2022 bridge explosion Russian milbloggers demanded retaliation.
Putin presented the 10 Oct 2022 infrastructure strikes as retaliation for the bridge; GUR said they had been planned earlier.
ISW argued Russia's use of scarce precision weapons on 10 Oct 2022 might cost it options elsewhere.
The same retaliation pattern followed Act 2, with Russia's Odesa port strikes of 18 Jul 2023.
Ukraine was coy about the Crimean Bridge in 2022.
Ukraine claimed both Crimean Bridge attacks in summer 2023; CNN describes Malyuk's direct claim as "an unusually direct bid to alert Moscow" to the drone threat.

cites.quote: an unusually direct bid to alert Moscow

text: Neizhpapa stressed "information silence" before the June 2025 Crimean Bridge strike.
ISW judged that the July 2023 strike would hit southern Russian logistics "in the midst of the ongoing Ukrainian counteroffensive".

cites.quote: in the midst of the ongoing Ukrainian counteroffensive

text: After Act 2 Russia chose physical barriers for the Crimean Bridge (sunken ferries, then barges, booms, nets and hedgehogs), put up with storm losses and rebuilt repeatedly.
Russia moved dangerous cargo off the Crimean Bridge onto ferries and ships.
Russia built the land railway through occupied territory as "redundancy" for the Crimean Bridge.
Once the Kerch ferries were destroyed in 2026, the Crimean Bridge again became "the critical remaining link".
Molfar argued in May 2024 that attacking the Crimean Bridge was no longer needed, since military rail traffic had stopped.
The SBU said "the bridge is doomed", and the Ukrainian Navy said the Crimean Bridge remained a target; Ukraine struck it again in 2025.
In 2025 Ukraine chose to go under the Crimean Bridge's surface barrier with charges placed over months; the sources do not explain the choice.
Russia called each Crimean Bridge attack terrorism against civilian infrastructure; Putin said Ukrainian special services "devised, carried out and ordered" Act 1.
Russia blamed HUR and Budanov for the 2022 bridge explosion, and in April 2023 a Moscow court issued an arrest warrant for Budanov.
In the Russian version of Act 1, the charge was about 10 t TNT equivalent of solid rocket fuel in 22.7 t of film reels, triggered by GPS at km 156.
Russia identified twelve people and detained eight in October 2022 over the bridge explosion.
Eight people were jailed for life in November 2025 after a closed trial for the 2022 Crimean Bridge bombing; all denied knowing what the cargo was.
Malyuk called the 22 people Russia jailed over the bridge "ordinary Russian smugglers".
notes: text gives 22 jailed here but eight detained/eight life sentences elsewhere; numbers refer to different counts

text: Meduza reported a Kremlin guide to the media on playing down the October 2022 Crimean Bridge damage.
The Russian Ministry of Transport claimed the July 2023 strike left the Crimean Bridge's rail bridge and road supports intact.
After Act 3 Peskov said there was "no damage" to the Crimean Bridge.
Russia claimed S-200s were downed at the Crimean Bridge on 12 Aug 2023 and presented the smoke as a deliberate screen; this was not independently verified.
Russia claimed three USVs were destroyed near the Crimean Bridge on 1–2 Sep 2023; this was not independently verified.
Russia claimed 12 ATACMS and five USVs (by helicopter) were downed near the Crimean Bridge on 15 Aug 2024; this was not independently verified.
Russia claimed a drone was shot down over the Crimean Bridge on 3 Jun 2025; this was not independently verified.
In 2022 Russian nationalist milbloggers criticised Putin's and Medvedev's silence after the Crimean Bridge explosion, following Medvedev's "red line" threats.
In 2023 Russian milbloggers faulted the neglect of maritime security at the Crimean Bridge in favour of checking cars.
Russia presented the 10 Oct 2022 missile strike and the 18 Jul 2023 Odesa strike as retaliation for the Crimean Bridge attacks.
The dossier's key Crimean Bridge coordinates are computed from OSM ways, with Nominatim used for named places.
